author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1969-01-01 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: How can thought know a thought greater than itself?
context_before: “Nought loves another as itself, Nor venerates another so. Nor is it possible to thought  A Greater than itself to know.”
context_after: How could you love another more than yourself? It is impossible, for there is no other.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from Christ Bears Our Sins (1969-01-01).

author: Neville Goddard

quote_original: You do not have yourself castrated.
context_after: You are simply beyond the organization of sex and your desire for earthly things ceases to be. Ninety-nine per cent of the people here desire worldly pleasures, while I speak of a pleasure that transcends this world – where one lives in a world of reality and creativity. But until that famine comes, you will continue to desire things that die in this world.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from Christ Bears Our Sins (1969-01-01).

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1969-01-01 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: I will go along with that.
context_before: This lady said that she is very fond of the Book of John, as it seems to be more loving than any other book in the Bible.
context_after: She felt that the answer to the experience I just spoke of would come to her from the Book of John. I suggest she read the 10th chapter of John. In it Christ is called a man who has a devil and they question why listen to him. You, my dear, are that central figure, and you are also the crowd screaming at yourself; and you deny the existence of the Christ within, for there is no other. There is only God.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from Christ Bears Our Sins (1969-01-01).
